scope: Read-only mapping of the supplied consolidated research to rejected or reopened integration items. No repository changes, new public-source verification, or import approval.
method: Compared every prior component by canonical JSON hash against all repository research JSON files.
Expanded every claim range in each explicit missing-URL/dataset hold and mapped the original component, claim ID, locator, source ID and literal catalogue URL.
Kept original not_applied reasons and separated source recovery from model, identity, date meaning and original-instrument gates.
Retained all source metadata as supplied; a URL or successful historical retrieval is not independent re-verification of its claim.

handoff_findings.finding: The three evidence archives were not a replacement for the consolidated research report/catalogue. Their README explicitly points to the consolidated JSON for the retained prior research and earlier source manifest.
handoff_findings.qualification: The integrators correctly reported what was missing from their three-archive input; the research had already been supplied separately in the consolidated JSON.

handoff_findings.finding: 32 of 66 prior structured components have no exact copy anywhere in repository research JSON; absence of a full component does not prove every individual fact is absent.
The supplied branch archive has a filename collision: branches/prior/claims.json contains the 26 logo claims, while the 279 branch claims survive in the consolidated JSON.
handoff_findings.attribution: Packaging error in our supplied archive, confirmed by parent audit of the original ZIP; not an integration overwrite.
handoff_findings.qualification: The prior handback-importable.json is present unchanged and still carries its importable branch evidence.

handoff_findings.finding: The prior 144-record branch batch was preserved but is absent from INTEGRATION.md merge commands.
handoff_findings.qualification: Parent independently simulated the merge with zero errors/warnings/conflicts and measured 24 undated out of 251, rather than 138. This audit does not rerun or authorize that merge.

handoff_findings.finding: C5 asks for 30 missing source URLs, but its 32 cited claims reference 25 distinct sources, all present in the consolidated catalogue.

R4E-C001: Public Accounts 1974/75 records an agreement dated 25 January 1974 under which the Province acquired Dunhill shares through Woodbridge Development Corporation. Qualification: Contemporary financial-statement evidence of the agreement date; the executed agreement itself has not been recovered.

R4E-C002: By 22 May 1974, the Province through Woodbridge had acquired sufficient Dunhill shares for Crown tax exemption. The next Public Accounts describes 22 May as the date it became a provincial Crown corporation. Qualification: This is not the date of incorporation or proof of direct 100% provincial share ownership on that day.

R4E-C003: After Woodbridge was wound up, Dunhill became wholly owned directly by the Province on 7 June 1974. Qualification: The financial note does not give a separate exact date for Woodbridge winding-up; do not assign June 7 as its legal dissolution date.

R4E-C004: The financial statements for the year ended 31 October 1974 identify eight wholly owned Dunhill subsidiaries: W.K.P. Construction Ltd.; Crown Lumber Limited; Fisher Developments Ltd.; Dunhill Homes Ltd.; Dunhill Holdings Ltd.; United Provincial Investments Ltd.; Ventures Realty Ltd.; Georgia Park Holdings Ltd. Qualification: Ownership observation in the consolidated statements, not the incorporation dates or first ownership dates of those subsidiaries. W.K.P. must not be silently equated with the original parent.

R4E-C005: The Housing Fund investment schedule reports all three issued Pemco common shares, cost $633,511, at both 31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976. Qualification: This establishes shareholding checkpoints, not the exact 1973 purchase date or a ministry accountability interval.

R4E-C007: The first-year financial statements state that the company was incorporated under the Canada Corporations Act on 5 May 1975 to operate Princess Marguerite. Qualification: Original financial-statement evidence; the federal certificate of incorporation itself was not obtained.

R4E-C008: The company acquired British Columbia Steamship Company Inc., a separate Washington corporation, on 15 May 1975. Qualification: Keep the federal Canadian company and Washington company as distinct legal entities.

R4E-C009: The company states that its share capital is held by five directors in right of the Province; the balance sheet lists five issued common shares. Qualification: A provincial beneficial-ownership observation, not evidence that the directors personally owned the company or proof of the responsible ministry.
R4E-C012: The original Act requires at least eight directors, appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council from persons holding elected municipal office.
R4E-C014: Section 4 of the original MTOC Act provides for at least seven directors appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

R4E-C016: The same 1982 amendment adds the express Crown-agent provision to the authority’s establishing section. Qualification: This claim concerns the express statutory agency clause, not a claim that no other Crown relationship existed before this date.

R4E-C019: The 1985 amendment’s new BC Transit Act section 2.1 transfers all MTOC property and rights to BC Transit and makes BC Transit liable for MTOC debts and obligations. The provision commenced on 1 June 1985. Qualification: A transfer/assumption event. The provision does not itself declare MTOC dissolved.

R4E-C021: OIC 1096/1985 appoints nine MTOC directors and its chair effective 1 June 1985, while OIC 1095 appoints the BC Transit board. Qualification: This is affirmative evidence against automatically treating the 1985 asset transfer as MTOC legal dissolution. Its ultimate legal end remains unproved.

R4E-C029: The Power Development Act 1961 vested BC Electric shares in the Crown and deemed the Act effective from 2 p.m. Pacific Standard Time, expressly excluding daylight saving time, on 1 August 1961. Qualification: This 1961 enactment was subsequently held ultra vires according to the contemporary Hydro report; the 1964 acquisition statute separately gives retroactive authority. Do not present the 1961 text as the whole legal story.

R4E-C031: OIC 840/1962 appoints the initial directors and appoints Gordon M. Shrum and Hugh L. Keenleyside co-chairmen. Qualification: Appointments under the original 1962 scheme; distinguish the later 1964 statutory authority.

R4E-C033: Hydro reports a settlement agreement dated 27 September 1963 with BC Power Corporation following the share valuation, and the Power Measures Act 1964 expressly ratifies that agreement. Qualification: Keep the settlement date separate from the original 1961 takeover date and later 1965 amalgamation.

R4E-C034: The BC Electric Company Limited Acquisition Act 1964 authorizes acquisition of all common shares as at 1 August 1961 for $197,114,358 and provides retroactive effect. Qualification: Enactment date is 20 March 1964; its operative acquisition date is deemed back to 1 August 1961. Preserve both fields.

R4E-C036: The 1964 Act makes the authority an agent of the Crown and makes the Minister of Finance its fiscal agent. Qualification: Fiscal-agent status is not proof that Finance held every aspect of ministerial responsibility for Hydro.
R4E-C037: The 1964 Act gives appointment of the authority’s directors to the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

R4E-C039: The agreement reproduced in the Power Measures Act 1966 takes effect at 5 p.m. local Vancouver time on 20 August 1965. The three bodies continue as the Hydro authority established under the 1964 Act, and BC Electric and the Power Commission cease separate corporate existence. Qualification: The ratifying Act assented on 1 April 1966 expressly validates the 20 August 1965 agreement. Do not date the amalgamation to the later assent.

R4E-C041: Power Measures Act 1966 section 5 deems the Crown-held BC Electric common shares surrendered to Hydro and cancelled immediately upon the amalgamation. Qualification: Statutory retroactive confirmation, assented to 1 April 1966.

R4E-C042: On 30 March 1993 the Minister of Transportation and Highways publicly acknowledged BC Rail’s recently completed Vancouver Wharves purchase. Qualification: A latest-confirmed date for the purchase, not the exact closing date or executed acquisition agreement.

R4E-C043: A July 1993 reprint expressly credited to BC Rail Coupler says Vancouver Wharves would remain a separate company with its own board and management after acquisition; 98 of its 111 acres were already leased from BC Rail. Qualification: Corporate announcement reproduced in a railway publication; useful contemporary governance evidence, but not a registry identity match or legal transfer instrument.

R4E-C045: Ministerial Order 5/2004, signed 30 December 2003, approves the BC Rail reorganization transactions; Schedule A(j) describes transfer of BC Rail Ltd.’s 75% interest in Vancouver Wharves Limited Partnership to BCRC or an affiliate. Qualification: Approval and planned transaction terms, not proof of closing. This is a limited-partnership interest, not 75% of an identically named company’s shares. The 2004 order number does not change the 2003 signature date.
